entry.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
entry.summary: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. Without altering the underlying architecture, we introduce History Representation, which integrates sparse visual keyframes with an explicit History Representation Map to preserve long-term spatiotemporal context. To effectively leverage this history, we further introduce History Utilization, a structured VQA supervision protocol comprising three categories: task-stage grounding, exploration consistency, and spatiotemporal target retrieval, enabling map-grounded reasoning and stable persistent long-horizon navigation. To fuel this system, we establish a complete annotation pipeline for monocular RGB videos and open-source a massive dataset featuring over 500 hours of high-quality real-world interactions and over 2,000 hours of annotated web videos. Trained mainly on the distribution of 1m height camera, Compass 1 generalizes seamlessly across diverse embodiments and scenarios, ranging from indoor environments to pedestrian-dense streets, spanning wheeled robot at 0.35m, quadruped dog at 0.5m, humanoid at 0.85m, and aerial drone at 1.5m. Compass 1achieves a dominant overall success rate of 79.4% across open-world evaluations, compared to 17.8% for the strongest baseline. It demonstrates exceptional zero-shot execution exceeding 90% on foundational tasks, a 250% boost in exploration, and an unparalleled leap from 0% to 58% in challenging persistent history backtracking.

entry.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
entry.summary: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

entry.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
entry.summary: Let $k$ be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension $F/k$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ_{F/k})$ satisfies $(1-β)\log d_F\ge c(k)$ with an effective constant $c(k)>0$, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions $K$ of $k$, in the form $h_K R_K \ge c(k)\, d_K^{1/2}/((2π)^{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\log d_K)$. Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem excluded the fields with quadratic subfields, since those subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field $k$, the first result removes this obstruction. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let $K/k$ be a Galois extension with group $G$, and suppose $S\subset G$ contains the identity. For any prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $k$, let $δ_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the proportion of the primes of $K$ above $\mathfrak{p}$ whose Frobenius lies in $S$. Then $\sum_{N\mathfrak{p}\le X}δ_{\mathfrak{p}}\,\log N\mathfrak{p}/N\mathfrak{p}\le(|S|/|G|+\varepsilon)\log X+O(1)$ holds uniformly in $K$ as soon as $X\ge d_K^{C}$, with $C$ and the implied constant depending only on $\varepsilon$, $C$, and the degree $[K:\mathbb{Q}]$. The proof is the argument of OpenAI in the form given by Kerr, simple vanishing at the points $(ιθ)_{ι\in S}$, with $θ$ in a box in $\mathcal{O}_K$, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be $[K:\mathbb{Q}]/|S|$ by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the determinant method gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.

entry.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
entry.summary: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

entry.title: Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
entry.summary: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincaré characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.

entry.title: CAPS: Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis for Missing MRI Imputation in Brain Tumor Segmentation
entry.summary: Multi-parametric MRI is the gold standard for neuro-oncology, yet acquiring complete 4-modality protocols may be unfeasible in real-world clinical practice. When handling missing modalities, existing automated systems force a critical compromise: robust segmenters operate as uninterpretable "black boxes" that bypass image generation, while standard synthesis models often produce blurry reconstructions lacking diagnostic reliability. To address this issue, we propose CAPS, a Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis framework that reconciles computational precision with clinical transparency. Our multi-modal generative architecture is driven by a hybrid objective function (L_1 + L_AFP + L_DualDice) that explicitly enforces the preservation of deep anatomical features and strict topological boundaries, rather than relying solely on pixel-wise optimization. Evaluated comprehensively on the BraTS Adult Glioma dataset, the framework achieves superior synthesis fidelity across intensity-based metrics, and demonstrates robust downstream segmentation performance (82.38% mean Dice), successfully restoring verifiable visual context. Furthermore, the framework exhibits exceptional zero-shot cross-domain generalization, maintaining high structural fidelity across completely unseen Meningioma, Pediatric, and Sub-Saharan African cohorts without domain-specific adaptation. Finally, a blinded radiological assessment confirms that our anatomy-aware approach significantly enhances both perceived image quality and clinical utility, providing clinicians with the reliable visual evidence required to trust downstream automated workflows.

entry.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
entry.summary: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

entry.title: A simpler proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros
entry.summary: This paper simplifies the recent OpenAI proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros.

entry.title: On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli
entry.summary: Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^γ$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

entry.title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
entry.summary: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;χ,ψ)$ and $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $χ_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;χ_{163},χ_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.

entry.title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
entry.summary: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $δ_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q\geδ_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $δ_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-β)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $χ$. A real zero close to one forces $χ(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

entry.title: Few small primes suffice to cover unit groups
entry.summary: Klurman, Shparlinski and Teräväinen showed that there is a set of at most $(\log Q)^{1+\varepsilon}$ primes of polylogarithmic size whose subset products cover the unit group $(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})^\times$ for almost all moduli $q\le Q$. We show that $(1/\log2+o(1))\log Q$ primes suffice, which is optimal to first order, since $m$ primes have at most $2^m$ subset products. The proof combines a doubling argument of Erdős--Rényi type for random subset products in a finite abelian group, modified to tolerate a small set of exceptional characters, with a one-time ``repair'' of the few primitive characters whose $L$-functions have zeros near $s=1$. An exact weighted repair gives a variant with at most $(2/\log2+o(1))\log Q$ primes and an exceptional set described explicitly.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages; verification code included as ancillary files

entry.title: Super Liouville theory on the torus: bootstrap and the super Virasoro minimal string
entry.summary: Motivated by applications to low-dimensional worldsheet string constructions, we analyze $\mathcal{N} = 1$ super Liouville theory on the torus. Specifically, we re-examine the recursive representations of the torus one-point super Virasoro blocks that have been constructed in the literature and correct several of their ingredients. In the process we identify a new block in the odd spin structure, associated with a privileged superdescendant whose torus one-point function transforms like that of a Virasoro primary. We then demonstrate that the structure constants for both spacelike and timelike super Liouville theory satisfy modular crossing. Furthermore, we use a bootstrap argument to construct modular crossing kernels for all four spin structure sectors, valid for central charges $c \in \mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,\tfrac{3}{2}]$, and verify that they correctly implement the crossing transformations of the blocks. As a concrete application of the technology, we analyze the super Virasoro minimal string. There are four such theories, $\mathrm{0A}^{\pm}$ and $\mathrm{0B}^{\pm}$, which are distinguished by the GSO projection together with the choice of worldsheet supercharge. The resulting NS-sector sphere three-point and torus one-point amplitudes are shown to agree with topological recursion on the spectral curves of the dual matrix integrals, which were recently derived from 3d supergravity. Notably, the one-point function of the privileged superdescendant plays an essential role in the contribution of the odd spin structure to the torus amplitude via a careful treatment of the picture changing operator. We also identify an exceptional zero-momentum Ramond insertion in the $\mathrm{0A}^{-}$ theory that we interpret geometrically as a Ramond puncture, and match its mixed sphere three-point amplitude to the corresponding intersection theory prediction.

entry.title: Prime-Detecting Identities from Dirichlet Inversion
entry.summary: For each integer k >= 1, let sigma_k(n) = sum_{d|n} d^k, let sigma_k^{-1} denote its Dirichlet inverse, and let J_k denote the kth Jordan totient function. Using established prime-power values of sigma_k^{-1}, we first obtain the elementary criterion sigma_k^{-1}(n) + J_k(n) + 2 = 0 precisely when n is prime. At k = 1, this involves Euler's totient J_1 = phi and provides a prime-only comparison for the next equation. Our main result classifies the zeros of sigma_k^{-1}(n) + mu(n) + J_k(n) + 3: for k = 1, they are precisely the primes and 18; for k >= 2, they are precisely the primes. The proof separates integers according to their prime-exponent patterns. Sign and divisibility arguments exclude composite zeros outside the cube-free nonsquarefree case, where an additional divisibility condition isolates 18 at k = 1 and precludes composite zeros for higher k. Standard convolution and Lambert-series identities provide the arithmetic framework, while an intermediate-divisor relation explains the exceptional zero. These criteria are structural characterizations rather than efficient primality tests, since direct evaluation of the multiplicative formulas generally presupposes a factorization of n.
